mentl/79a82dd:
An oracle-blind probe of record spread — the constructive dual of the record
rest fixed at the last two pins — found the surface sound and found a hazard
one layer under it.

Spread measured sound on every probe: the value runs, each field read alone
answers its own (a=1, b=2, c=3, d=4 through a spread that re-sorts all four),
the field TYPE survives (`s.a ++ "x"` is E_TypeMismatch), and the effect ROW
survives (an effectful closure spread and then called under `!E` refuses).
tests/syntax/record-spread-resort pins the layout half at 49 with distinct
power-of-two weights, so a slot confusion changes the answer rather than
hiding in it.

The hazard is the exit channel. Measured against the pinned boot: a `main`
returning 124 or 125 exits with that number, and 126, 127, 128, 200, 255 and
256 all exit 1. A fixture cannot encode a value above 125, and the author who
writes one reads `exit=1` — which says the program computed 1, and it did
not. The next move after that reading is to "fix" the expectation to 1 and
bank a gate that asserts nothing.

The battery was audited against the ceiling in the same pass: 157 fixtures
carry a numeric expectation, 9 sit above it, and every one of those is 134 —
a wasm trap through SIGABRT, a different channel from a returned value, and
still distinguishable (a value of 134 arrives as 1). Nothing landed was
broken; the hazard was prospective.

run-micro.sh refuses 126 and 127 before running, since neither is a reachable
value nor a signal, and on a failure where the expectation exceeds 125 and
the run returned 1 it says the 1 is the channel and not the program.
Falsified four ways: both new paths fire, a normal fixture is untouched, and
a trap fixture still passes at 134.

No wheel change, so no march; the pin is unmoved at c968f690567b.

mentl/79c2ac7:
The IndexExpr sugar arm bound its receiver with graph_bind — a direct
cell overwrite that discarded the receiver's proven TList(elem) and
orphaned a fresh element class at every subscript, while its sibling
seq_force one table over states the law in its own comment: "Force =
UNIFY, never overwrite. graph_bind would DISCARD the arg's proven type."
The list_index call form always unified; only the xs[i] sugar had the
discard-mint.

This was the union-find fracture beneath the monomorphization free-leaf
rule. An adversarial worktree agent probe-pinned it: merge's condition
subscripts (xs[0] <= ys[0]) rooted at 13777 while its param element
rooted at 13793 — the condition-position values flow only into the Bool
and never rejoin, so the orphan class persists; return-position
subscripts healed back through ++. The agent verified the fix collapses
the classes to one root. The orchestrator's own hypothesis —
instantiate-shares-never-clones as the root — was refuted by the same
probes: instantiate heals through argument unification, polymorphic
recursion included. The label died to the artifact.

Both forces now unify: the receiver against an expected TList(elem), the
index against TInt (line 881 had the same overwrite). The §4① String
seam is preserved: a proven-TString receiver satisfies the force (a
String is a sequence) and s[i] binds TByte — sharper than the old
clobber-to-TList. Unlocked and named in the ledger: the exact root-keyed
substitution replacing the free-leaf approximation, and the
multi-type-generic guard lift.

TRANSITION m3 == m4 (the sharper classes cross one generation through
the wheel's own subscripts); boot re-pinned da45bcdd, self-confirming
the clean m2 == m3. Census 0, frontier 153/0, proof-exactness 9/9,
crown 5/5, micros green.
mentl/79cc7b5:
buf.data and buf.count are two reads of buf, not two consumes —
infer_field_access_record consumed the receiver at every field access, so a
record whose fields are read more than once (Buffer{data: push(buf.data, x),
count: buf.count + 1}) floored E_OwnershipViolation. Reading .field never
moves the record.

The receiver is bracketed in a borrow scope when it is a value chain — a
VarRef or a nested field access — so the whole chain down to the base binding
is a borrow. A call receiver (f(x).field) keeps its normal inference, so x's
move into f still consumes. Carried-Truth: the graph knows a field read is a
read; the ledger treated it as a move.

Census 583 -> 582; buffer.mn's buf.data/buf.count cleared, soundness intact
(a real double-move is still caught), clean m2 == m3 transition. Residue (4):
the call-arg-borrow — an `own` value passed to a borrowing parameter
(len(nodes), list_set(overlay_bufs)) — the last move-vs-borrow piece, which
reads the callee's param ownership at each argument.
mentl/79e614a:
infer_seq_op typed the functor projections by a name-keyed table that
re-derived each op's argument order and forced arg types by overwrite.
Two faults compounded into the m3 flatten/++ trap.

fold and take had scrambled arg slots: fold(init, f, xs) was typed as
(xs, init, f) and take(n, xs) as (xs, n), so the flowing datum landed on
the wrong parameter. And seq_force/seq_force_fn used graph_bind, which
overwrites a node's type rather than unifying it, so fold([], ...) lost
that [] is a list and the accumulator never learned [a]. flatten's
acc ++ xs then read a bare TVar at emit and floored to (unreachable).

Read the arg slots from the one real signature (prelude.mn), and make
"force" mean unify: mint the expected type and unify the arg's root with
it, so the constraint propagates into a lambda's params and an empty
literal's element. The representation of ++ is now a projection of the
proven accumulator type: str_concat when the init is "", list_concat
when it is [].

Rungs 8/0, micros-through-m2 45/45; m3 assembles and the trap marches
from effect_type_vars to lower's ls_bind_local.

mentl/7953d2f:
Adds row.wat — full Boolean algebra over effect rows per spec 01 +
Hβ §1.10. Substrate primitive #4 (Effect row algebra). + (union),
- (diff), & (intersection), Pure (identity); ! / Neg + Sub + Inter
constructors are present, normalization to canonical form is the
named follow-up.

Also extends str.wat with $str_compare (lex-order byte-by-byte
compare returning -1/0/1) — required by row.wat's sorted-name-set
ops; bundled in this commit per Anchor 7 "land whole" (str_compare
exists only to support row.wat name-set ordering).

Architecture:
  - EfPure as sentinel i32 = 150 (< HEAP_BASE; nullary-sentinel
    discipline per Hβ §1.5).
  - Fielded variants (record tags 151-155):
      EfClosed(names) — tag 151, arity 1; field_0 = name list ptr
      EfOpen(names, handle) — tag 152, arity 2; field_0 = names,
                              field_1 = rowvar handle (i32)
      EfNeg(inner) — tag 153, arity 1; field_0 = inner row
      EfSub(left, right) — tag 154, arity 2
      EfInter(left, right) — tag 155, arity 2
  - Tag region 150-179 (private; avoids graph.wat 50-99 + env.wat
    130-149 + TokenKind 0-44 + closure tags by Hβ.lower).
  - Name lists: flat lists of string pointers (str.wat layout),
    sorted lex by $str_compare, deduplicated. Constructors don't
    re-sort (Tier-3 base; Hβ.infer constructs canonical form).

Exports (~25 functions):
  Constructors:
    $row_make_pure / closed / open / neg / sub / inter
  Predicates + accessors:
    $row_tag, $row_is_pure / closed / open, $row_names, $row_handle
  Name-set helpers (sorted-lex flat list ops):
    $name_set_contains, $name_set_eq, $name_set_subset,
    $name_set_union, $name_set_inter, $name_set_diff (all preserve
    canonical form; sorted merges in O(na+nb))
  Algebra:
    $row_union (E + F per spec 01),
    $row_diff (E - F),
    $row_inter (E & F),
    $row_subsumes (B ⊆ F per spec 01 §Subsumption — gates handler
                   install at compile time + the four compilation
                   gates Pur
mentl/7949a07:
Phase B: query.lux forensic substrate (first Mentl tentacle)
  - std/compiler/query.lux: Question/QueryResult ADTs, parse_query,
    answer(), render_result(). v1 bridge using env_lookup/apply.
  - examples/query_bootstrap.lux: stdin-based entry point.
  - bootstrap/Makefile: query build targets.

Phase C: v2 compiler core from specs (the rebuild)
  All 9 files in std/compiler/v2/ built directly from the 12
  executable specs in docs/rebuild/00-11:

  - graph.lux: SubstGraph (spec 00). Flat-array, epoch-tagged,
    O(1) chase. SubstGraphRead/Write effect split IS the one-writer
    invariant. No linked-list subst chains.

  - effects.lux: EffRow Boolean algebra (spec 01). + - & ! over
    effect rows. Four compilation gates (Pure, !IO, !Alloc, !Network)
    fall out of one mechanism. Normalization, subsumption, handler
    absorption.

  - types.lux: Ty + Reason + Scheme + typed AST + all effects
    (specs 02, 03, 06). TRefined, TCont, TParam with Ownership,
    Span, Node, all 14 effects declared.

  - infer.lux: HM + let-generalization, one walk (spec 04). Writes
    directly to SubstGraph. No subst argument threading. Hazel-style
    error holes. Instantiation via FreshHandle effect.

  - lower.lux: Live-observer lowering (spec 05). LookupTy effect
    chases graph. No TUnit fallback. No val_concat. Monomorphism
    check is a graph read.

  - pipeline.lux: Single-walk entry, all handlers composed. Query
    as first-class handler. Diagnostic, Env, Graph, Verify, LookupTy
    all installed here.

  - own.lux: Ownership as effect (spec 07). Consume effect + affine
    ledger. Ref-escape checking.

  - verify.lux: Verify ledger (spec 02). Accumulates obligations,
    no solving. Arc F.1 swaps to verify_smt.

  - clock.lux: Clock family (spec 11). Four peer time effects,
    four handler tiers each.

This is the final form built directly. The wheel defined in the specs;
the engine built to meet it. No v1 iteration, no patches.

bits/794c9c9:
Mouths grow shapes: the voice track pairs RMS loudness with zero-
crossing rate per hop and classifies closed, small, wide, fricative
slit, and round; deterministic from the PCM, so render and preview
agree. Spectral-class, not phoneme-class, and honestly labeled as such;
the drawMouth geometry switches on the class.

Pins bend paper: PIN events are control points for moving-least-
squares similarity deformation (Schaefer 2006, the closed-form member
of the ARAP family; interpolation at controls proven in tests), drawn
as a textured triangle mesh with seam-hiding inflation. Pins simulate
as spring points that ride the body and chase performed targets, so a
grabbed pin is one more pass channel next to bodies and pieces. Pins
and snips are exclusive per puppet: cut paper or bend it, never both.

Body passes: MediaPipe pose from the front camera turns wrists into
virtual grabs, one hand per assigned target, mirrored for selfie
sense, recorded as ordinary passes with the camera in a corner PiP.
The pose model stages next to the segmenter and runtime-caches.

Bits travel: exportBundle packs the recipe and every referenced asset
into one .bit.json; the bits list opens one and the whole show is
yours to re-perform. 33 unit tests; the e2e fixture adds a pinned
puppet with a pin pass.
